Lines.Text: TAP... DRAG, TAP...
The station's cold, white marble corridor.
Moments ago, the five girls had moved as though they could tear a stage apart. Now they walked like a defeated army.
Ria and Hana struggled to support Jiwoo between them, her ankle swollen.
Blood ran from Seoyun's scraped knee as she stared vacantly ahead.
Red seeped through the tape around Mina's ankle too, leaving small stains on the marble.
Beyond the corridor, the next group's bright music and the audience's cheers reverberated like phantom noise.
At the head of that desolate procession, P bit his lip bloody and shouted into his phone.
Compensation? Director, are you kidding me?! My girls got hurt!
They kept singing with their own voices after you cut the music, and your staff threw them around like luggage!
Oh, for God's sake, P. Are you even listening?
We're offering double the cancellation penalty.
S-Tier threatened to pull their entire lineup. What do you expect me to do? Shut the station down?
This isn't about the money! Do you have any idea what they went through for those three and a half minutes—
P. Enough romance. Face reality. Who wants to watch girls from that garbage agency of yours dance?
You were filler. Bad for the ratings. I took pity on you, and look at the mess you've made.
Take the money while I'm still offering and go away quietly.
BEEP. BEEP. BEEP.
The call ended before he could answer.
Still gripping his shattered phone, P drove his forehead into the cold corridor wall.
A garbage agency. Filler that dragged down the ratings.
Inside the fortress money had built, the miracle they had carved from their own bodies was filth—something that could be paid a few coins and swept away whenever convenient.
That was when it happened.
Then brisk, imperious footsteps broke the crushing silence from the other end of the hall.
CLICK. CLICK. CLICK.
Flawless hair styled at an exclusive salon. Stage outfits and diamond accessories dazzling enough to hurt the eyes.
Surrounded by a wall of staff and managers, S-Tier's flagship girl group walked down the corridor. At that moment, no group in Korea was bigger.
At the front of the glittering procession walked Joo-hee, wearing a leisurely smile.
At the sight of her, the dazed girls went rigid.
Expensive perfume smothered the air around them, overpowering the sweat, blood, and basement mold.
The S-Tier idols covered their noses and giggled at the dirt on Jiwoo and Mina, as if looking at something unclean.
(retreating behind a manager, openly grimacing) Ew, who are they? I can smell blood. They let beggars into the station now?
Oh, those must be the rejects we dumped.
I think I've seen them before. Why are they still crawling around here? Have some dignity.
None of the girls could answer.
Mina bowed her head and bit her lip until it bled. Silent tears fell from Seoyun's blank eyes.
Jiwoo clutched her aching ankle and covered her mouth. Hana could only tremble, afraid even to breathe.
At the open mockery, something murderous flashed in Ria's eyes.
She clenched her fists, ready to lunge, but P quickly stretched out an arm to stop her.
If a confrontation started here, only the powerless girls would pay for it.
Move, Kang Joo-hee.
(with a revoltingly sympathetic smile) See, P? I told you to stay quietly by my side.
You forgot your place, got thrown out, and this is all you have to show for it?
(looking down coldly at the silent girls, clicking her tongue) Poor things. Taken in by P's little hero act, rotting in that stinking basement.
Look. While your precious shield gets trampled and begs on his knees, my girls walk in the spotlight.
Her words cut too close to the truth for anyone to answer.
P stood with torn trousers and ruined shoes, freshly kicked by the crew. Joo-hee stood protected by a retinue. The contrast was unbearable.
P, I've had some money sent over as compensation. Use it for their medical bills.
And keep them away from my girls' stage from now on.
She swept back her hair and turned without a second thought. Her glittering idols followed,
leaving laughter behind. P and the girls stood frozen like ghosts until that procession of predators vanished toward the brilliant stage.
Until that procession of predators vanished toward the brilliant stage,
P and the girls stood frozen like ghosts.
A cramped communal waiting room in a forgotten corner of the station. It did not even have a nameplate.
P opened the door. Supporting one another, the five girls came in and sank onto the sofa in the dark.
No one spoke.
Despair pressed down too heavily for even a word of comfort.
In the silent room, only the wall-mounted television was on.
And now, the act you've all been waiting for! From S-Tier...!
On the live broadcast...
The same main stage they had just been dragged from like baggage.
The S-Tier idols from the corridor danced beneath brilliant lights and lavish special effects.
The audience chanted their names in a frenzy.
The most perfect, dazzling paradise money could make.
And exiled from it, five invisible people sat on a sofa in the dark, arms around bloodied knees, staring blankly up at the screen.
The television's bright light shone cruelly into their hollow eyes.
That night, every one of them understood, deep in their bones, that no amount of effort could overcome this enormous violence.
